1. Competition pool overflow channels and balance tank necks, including grating supports, access covers and all inlet sleeves. Carry the membrane through each recessed channel corner and seal the interfaces with pool circulation fittings;

3. Staff housing utility balconies and washing machine recesses, including outlet sumps, hose taps and movement joints;
 Extend the membrane beneath the appliance plinths and over every balcony threshold before installing the wearing surface;
4. Basement fire service tank floors and wall junctions, including pipe entry seals, access ladders and construction joints. Protect the completed membrane during installation of the maintenance platform supports;
5. Irrigation storage cistern and pump enclosure, including overflow sleeves, equipment anchors and the door sill. Seal every cable gland and provide waterproof returns around the removable pump access cover;
6. West gate planter troughs and adjoining paving channels, including root barrier junctions, drain baskets and irrigation penetrations. Join the membrane continuously around each trough end and protect it before placing soil;
7. Roofless service yard washdown trenches and trapped sumps, including cover frames and crossings beneath the vehicle route;
 Continue the membrane at each trench intersection and use compatible seals where the yard joints meet the drainage channel;
8. Accessible toilet compartments and cleaning cupboards, including grab rail fixings, sanitary penetrations and the mop sink upstand. Carry the waterproofing across the doorway junctions and beneath fixed cupboard bases;
9. Basement retaining wall drainage pockets and lift pit tanking, including kicker joints, sump recesses and embedded service sleeves. Protect the tanking from reinforcement damage and leave the specified drainage inspection points accessible.

Schedule W ends with entry 9. No other installation area is added by the separate finish warranty decisions, which will be issued on 18 September.

Adopted Bills and quantity status

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R203 Date 2026-09-03 Email reply

From: Fictional Quantity Surveyor <qs@consense-scenario.invalid>
To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

Use the BQ plus SOR pricing scheme. The adopted schedule contains seven parent Bills, listed below in issue order. Numbering restarts in each pricing namespace, so the two entries numbered 1 are distinct Bills and the two entries numbered 2 are distinct Bills.

Bill No. | Formal description | Pricing namespace
1 | Air Conditioning and Mechanical Ventilation | SOR
2 | Lift and Escalator Plant | SOR
1 | General Requirements | BQ
2 | Workmanship Preambles | BQ
3 | Bored Piles and Basement Foundations | BQ
4 | Indoor Sports Hall and Staff Quarters | BQ
5 | Site Formation and Drainage (All Provisional) | BQ

All BQ quantities are provisional, including the quantities in BQ Bills 1, 2, 3, 4 and 5. No BQ quantity is fixed for payment. The SOR Bills are rate schedules. The qualifier in the formal BQ Bill 5 title is retained; it does not restrict the provisional status to that Bill.

The Bill collection pages and contents index are supporting sheets. The seven rows above exhaust the parent Bill identities; no supporting sheet creates an additional Bill.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

Construction scope and concrete production decisions

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R204 Date 2026-09-04 Meeting minutes

Attendees: Fictional Project Architect, Structural Engineer, Procurement Officer and Quantity Surveyor. Recorder: Fictional Quantity Surveyor.

Works Subject to Excision are specified for the ancillary stores. The contract includes site formation works. An Excavation Permit is required because drainage connections will be excavated within the public road.

Subsidised Sale Flats production is excluded. Neither exhibition flats nor show flats are required; select no exhibition or show flat provision.

The domestic staff block uses conventional in situ construction. CON8 volumetric precast components are not used. PSE submissions for CON8 modules are therefore outside this project.

The Tender is based on in situ concrete facades, not on precast concrete facades. Precast facades are not permitted under APE2.A410 for this project.

The WTO Government Procurement Agreement does not apply to this tender.

Foundation design settlement and tender design obligations

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R205 Date 2026-09-07 Email reply

From: Fictional Quantity Surveyor <qs@consense-scenario.invalid>
To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

The foundation designs belong to the Architect, who has completed the piling, pilecap and footing designs. The Contractor carries out the foundation works but is not responsible for designing them. No Contractor designed foundations are included.

No Contractor design is established at Tender acceptance. The settled permanent foundation designs are the Architect's designs, not a Contractor design proposal. Tenderers are not required to submit a proposed foundation design with the Tender.

This reply settles foundation design duties only. It is not the overall component schedule: the separate acoustic screen works and all component work limits will appear in the responsibility register issued on 11 September.

Whether a design related quotation should precede a Variation instruction remains undecided. No approval or rejection of that optional requirement is recorded here.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

Tender submission method and document issue

To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

The adopted tendering procedure is the two-envelope system. Place the technical submission and the priced offer in separate sealed envelopes for the same tender.

For BQ issue, use Hardcopy printed originals. This is the adopted BQ format. L10Pro is used solely for a reference copy of the SOR schedules, whose official issue and subsequent pricing addenda are also Hardcopy. A reference copy does not alter the adopted BQ issue.

The photocopy charge is HK$7.35 per missing tender copy page measuring A3 or smaller. The photocopy rate for a page larger than A3 has not been decided.

The conventional two-envelope procedure has no additional alternative tendering arrangement in this project. Return media do not define the issue format of the pricing documents.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R209 Date 2026-09-11 Email reply

From: Fictional Quantity Surveyor <qs@consense-scenario.invalid>
To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

The following register replaces the earlier foundation-only description as the exhaustive schedule of component responsibilities. The four rows cover every component for this contract. In each row, the design column refers to Contractor design and the construction column refers to Contractor execution. An Architect designed component has No in the Contractor design column.

Contractor designs | Actual work scope | Component | Contractor constructs
No | Small freestanding garden sign plinths | footings | Yes
No | Plant room acoustic screen supports | other | Yes
No | Staff block pile caps | pilecaps | Yes
No | Sports hall bored piles | piling | Yes

The listed footings are exclusively for small freestanding garden signboards. They do not serve a building or any major external structure.

RSE endorsed submissions are required under the structural submission provisions.

The full additional tender submission list consists of these three entries:
Submit an RSE endorsed temporary excavation support scheme.
Submit an occupied staff housing access management plan.
Submit a road drainage connection sequencing proposal.

The register confirms the foundation duties already settled on 7 September. No Contractor design assignment has been introduced and no fifth component is omitted from this register.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R211 Date 2026-09-15 Meeting minutes

Attendees: Fictional Project Architect, Structural Engineer, Procurement Officer and Quantity Surveyor. Recorder: Fictional Quantity Surveyor.

The adopted sectional schedule is set out below. These three designations are the entire Section schedule.
Works types | Location | Section designation
demolition | Detached obsolete stores at the southern parcel | Section 1
building, foundation | Sports hall at the northern parcel | Section 2
building, foundation | Staff housing at the western parcel | Section 3

The demolition site is the southern parcel. The building sites are the northern and western parcels. Building and demolition sites are separated; no parcel contains both types of work.

Use SCC8.302 for weather extension of time. SCC8.303 is not adopted, so its demolition-only Section insertion is not applicable.

Adopt the late possession provision. The additional loss provision is not adopted; neither a specified Section list nor a relevant Section for that optional provision is to be inserted.

parts.sourceText:
Other installations and payment provisions

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R214 Date 2026-09-18 Email reply

From: Fictional Quantity Surveyor <qs@consense-scenario.invalid>
To: Fictional Coordination Team <team@consense-scenario.invalid>

Roofing installation is excluded from this work package; the roofing installation warranty detail is not applicable. Refuge floor installation is included in the staff housing block, but no refuge floor installation warranty is required.

The adopted finish warranty decisions are as follows. An acrylic paint warranty is not required. A wall tiling warranty is required. An epoxy coated cast iron pipe installation warranty is required.

Play equipment and Impact Absorbing Surfacing Materials are both excluded from these works.

The SCC14.305 advance payment arrangement is not adopted. Its repayment period and first deduction certificate have no application in this tender. The whole contract completion period remains 45 months.

These equipment, finish and payment decisions leave all nine entries in Schedule W and its other waterproofing warranty effective.

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

Regards,
Fictional Quantity Surveyor

Outstanding decisions and final tender record

This is a fictional tender coordination exercise. All persons, organisations, proceedings and project decisions in this correspondence are invented. It has no contractual effect.

Record R215 Date 2026-09-21 Meeting minutes

Attendees: Fictional Project Architect, Structural Engineer, Procurement Officer and Quantity Surveyor. Recorder: Fictional Quantity Surveyor.

The unresolved register contains four matters only: the photocopy rate above A3, the Project Architect telephone number, the site inspection end date, and whether a design related quotation is required before instructing a Variation. We have no adopted value for any of these four matters. They remain for the business reviewer to determine.

The existing replies remain effective. The seven type qualified parent Bills, four component rows, two protected trees, nine waterproofing areas and three Sections are exhaustive for this tender. There is no additional trade, component or scope list in these minutes.

All extracted entries are proposed prefills. The business reviewer must adopt the applicable entries before generating the contract documents.
